foreign_system.name: Docker Engine / BuildKit / Buildx
foreign_system.authority: Docker official CLI and BuildKit documentation
foreign_system.role: container execution, image storage, build-cache realization and reclaim

purpose: Treat Docker capacity as schedulable physical state. Prefer archive/history eviction and BuildKit-aware least-recently-used cache reclamation over low-free-space hard stops, while keeping persistent volume deletion a distinct authority class.

observations.note: Docker documents JSON formatting for daemon disk-usage summary.
Buildx emits newline-delimited JSON records. Raw descriptions are diagnostic input, not ResourceGraph identity.

inactive_image_store.note: Docker Desktop classic and containerd image stores are distinct. Switching stores can leave the inactive store consuming disk while its images and containers are hidden from the active store view.

prune_surfaces.scheduler_preference: Use --min-free-space to express ResourceGraph reserve goals and let BuildKit evict least-recently-used records. Use --reserved-space as the hard cache floor rather than deleting cache indiscriminately.

prune_surfaces.volume_boundary: Volumes are outside the default prune. Volume deletion remains a separately admitted persistent-state effect.

v3_docker_capacity_policy.principle: Docker/build capacity is more valuable than retaining reconstructable local archaeology.
ordered_reclaim: superseded Bonfyre/Aurekai archives and historical campaign bulk
language/package caches and generated build products
BuildKit reclaimable shared records when required to reach reserve
anonymous/named volume state only under separate persistent-state authority
v3_docker_capacity_policy.note: The concrete command is an EffectKernel candidate, not an unconditional startup command. ResourceWeather should first observe reclaimability and current free-space state.

admission_rules: A Docker-heavy WorkNode should include predicted image/build-context/cache growth in its resource envelope.
When free space is below target but BuildKit reports enough reclaimable cache, prefer BuildKit GC over rejecting the WorkNode.
A non-reclaimable BuildKit record is not promoted to deletable merely because Bonfyre is under pressure.
A named volume is persistent state even when unused by a currently running container; do not treat 'unused' as equivalent to 'reconstructable'.
A completed containerized WorkNode should leave a compact receipt identifying image/build inputs and effect outputs so stopped containers can be disposable realization state.
ResourceWeather must distinguish physical bytes from sums over shared cache records; record sums are evidence/features, not necessarily filesystem accounting.
factor_validity_triggers: major Docker/BuildKit upgrade changing disk-usage or prune semantics

solved_invariants: Docker volumes are not ordinary build cache.
BuildKit reclaimability is foreign evidence that must be observed, not guessed from path names.
Free-space targets can be expressed to BuildKit directly with --min-free-space.
Shared BuildKit records may affect multiple builds and should remain distinguishable from private records.
Inactive Docker Desktop image stores can consume capacity while being invisible from the active image-store view.
regression_fences: Do not gate all Docker work on a fixed free-space threshold when reclaimable BuildKit capacity exists.
Do not run volume deletion as an implicit consequence of ordinary docker system prune.
Do not interpret a BuildKit record-size sum as exact physical disk usage when shared records are present.
Do not let a Docker storage-backend switch invalidate ResourceWeather silently.
